newsitem.title: UK: P&O sees no need for UK review of Stena deal.
newsitem.headline: P&O sees no need for UK review of Stena deal.

text.p: British construction, property and shipping group P&O said on Thursday it saw no reason for the UK decision to refer its planned channel ferry merger with units of Sweden's Stena Line AB for monopolies investigation.

In a statement the company called the referal "totally unnecessary", adding it saw a clear connection with the current operating difficulties being experienced by the ferries' main rival Eurotunnel's Channel Tunnel after last week's fire.
"Although the tunnel is temporarily out of action due to the unfortunate fire, I cannot see how the MMC reference will change the underlying situation," chairman Lord Sterling said.
"It has now been kicked into touch for another three months," he added, noting that the Monopolies and Mergers Commission had until March 6, 1997 to complete its study.

P&O and Stena argue that their alliance is a response to the rapid emergence of Eurotunnel SA/Plc's as the market leader for transport across the busy short-sea stretch between Dover, England and Calais, France.
Eurotunnel has said it understands the ferries motivation for cooperating and would welcome a deal if it led to a reduction in the capacity offered on the transport corridor.

P&O said in today's statement, "Although Eurotunnel has a short term problem, the fact remains that it has already taken some 45 percent of the market and can soon be expected to return to at least this level of operation."

"It is therefore difficult to see that there is any competition concern that requires investigation. In the meantime, the future benefits to consumers of the proposed merger cannot be realised," the company added.
Share analysts echoed P&O's implication that the tunnel's operating problems had been part of the reasoning for the referral, and said they saw it largely as a temporary setback.
